author: RipLey Simone
title: Office of Resilience opens offices for Hurricane Helene recovery efforts - NewsBreak
text:
By RipLey Simone ,
4 hours ago
SPARTANBURG, S.C. (WSPA) – The South Carolina Office of Resilience is opening four new offices across the Upstate to help communities with recovery efforts from Hurricane Helene.
On Wednesday September 24, the Region 2 office in Spartanburg opened, and will serve residents in Spartanburg, Laurens, Union, Chester, York, and Cherokee counties.
Kevin O’Dell, the Public Information Coordinator for the Office of Resilience, said opening the new offices allows them to better reach residents in need of assistance.
“We’ll be able to address a lot of unmet needs caused by Hurricane Helene,” O’Dell said. “From a disaster case management perspective, those needs can vary greatly. They can be housing related, they can be physical, financial, or even emotional.”
Map of Disaster Case Management Regional Offices from SC Office of Resilience Previously, the Office of Resilience met residents on the road to learn of their needs through mobile intakes, which involved people submitting applications for assistance at community access points like libraries. With the new space, residents will be able to walk in to an office and receive assistance from a disaster case manager, with or without an appointment.
The mobile intake events will still continue around region 2, according to O’Dell, and the schedule can be found here .
The Office of Resilience started as a disaster recovery agency in response to the 2015 floods.
“[We] exist to lessen the impact of disasters on the citizens and communities of South Carolina through statewide resilience planning and coordination, hazard mitigation, and long-term disaster recovery,” O’Dell explained. “We’ve successfully completed three recovery programs using those funds, and Hurricane Helene will be number four.”
Some of the funding the Office of Resilience uses for recovery efforts are from a disaster case management program grant from FEMA.
After natural disasters, FEMA will determine the amount of cash assistance to provide to individual survivors based on needs. The Office of Resilience differs by not issuing cash directly to survivors, but addressing their needs at no cost.
“What we will do is work to address their needs at no cost to the survivor. So if we are able to serve them through our housing recovery programs, we will work directly with contractors to make sure that the repairs or the replacement are done. And the survivor does not have to in any way get involved with the financials of that.”
O’Dell said this also helps them address a wider variety of needs that other disaster relief agencies may not cover.
